text: Quickstart · Benchmarks · Docs · Kernels · Blog post · runanywhere.ai TrnRT is an open inference engine for large language models on AWS Trainium. It serves an OpenAI-compatible API from one trn2.48xlarge , runs decode as NKI megakernels (about one kernel per layer half), and keeps a prefix cache across device and host memory. GLM-5.3-Flash is the first supported model; more open models are on the way. How we built it, with the AgentX results: Serving GLM-5.3-Flash on one Trainium2 box with NKI layer megakernels . You need Docker, a trn2.48xlarge to serve on, and any x86_64 host to compile on. New to Trainium? Start with docs/AWS.md . 1. Build the image (Neuron SDK 2.32 (neuronx-cc 2.27), Python 3.13) git clone https://github.com/RunanywhereAI/trnrt.git && cd trnrt docker build -f docker/Dockerfile \ --build-arg TRNRT_VERSION= $( python3 -c ' import trnrt; print(trnrt.__version__) ' ) \ --build-arg TRNRT_REVISION= $( git rev-parse HEAD ) -t trnrt . 2. Build the compile cache (any x86_64 host, no NeuronCore needed; takes hours) OUT=/data/trnrt REV=eb9eb208eb0d988989d07a6a12d0fdeb5f52574a mkdir -p $OUT /nki $OUT /work trnrt () { docker run --rm -e HF_TOKEN -v $OUT : $OUT \ -v $OUT /nki:/var/tmp/nki-intermediate-cache trnrt " $@ " ; } trnrt compile shapes zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --revision $REV --out $OUT trnrt compile decisions --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --revision $REV --out $OUT trnrt compile capture --out $OUT -- --model $OUT /shapes trnrt compile compile --out $OUT --work-root $OUT /work trnrt compile strip --out $OUT 3. Serve (on the trn2.48xlarge , with $OUT/cache and $OUT/nki copied over) hf download zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --revision eb9eb208eb0d988989d07a6a12d0fdeb5f52574a \ --local-dir /models/GLM-5.3-Flash docker run --rm --privileged --network host --ipc=host \ -v /data/trnrt/cache:/cache \ -v /data/trnrt/nki:/var/tmp/nki-intermediate-cache \ -v /models/GLM-5.3-Flash:/model \ -e NEURON_LIBTORCH_CACHE_ROOT=/cache \ trnrt serve --model /model --port 8000 4. Call it with any OpenAI client from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI ( base_url = "http://localhost:8000/v1" , api_key = "unused" ) reply = client . chat . completions . create ( model = "glm" , messages = [{ "role" : "user" , "content" : "Write a haiku about Trainium." }], extra_body = { "session_id" : "my-session" }, # keeps a conversation on one engine's prefix cache ) print ( reply . choices [ 0 ]. message . content ) The full guide covers what each step needs, start-up checks, the batch 4, 8 and 12 configurations and every flag: deploy · API · configuration . GLM-5.3-Flash is where TrnRT starts. The engine, router, caches and compile pipeline are built to carry more model families, and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md describes what a new one needs. SemiAnalysis AgentX replays real coding-agent sessions. One trn2.48xlarge ran it at a 1M-token context with 32 concurrent agents, for one hour per point: Tokens count input (cached input included) and output. Spot price: $8.60/h, us-east-2, 3 Nov 2026. On a capacity block at $35.76/h, the batch 12 cost is $0.167 per million tokens. Full tables, cold-prompt latencies, long prompts and methodology are in docs/RESULTS.md . These numbers were measured with an earlier build of TrnRT. This repository passes these checks against that build ( docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md ): Decode is not limited by memory bandwidth here; small instructions, kernel boundaries and exposed collectives dominate it. So each decode megakernel follows three rules: keep the working set in SBUF, use both physical cores symmetrically, and move the collectives into the kernel. docs/MEGAKERNELS.md walks through every kernel. trnrt/ ├── __main__.py CLI: serve, engine, compile ├── serve/ OpenAI API, session-affine router, output parsers ├── engine/ scheduler, prefix caches, tensor parallelism ├── models/ GLM-5.3-Flash: KDA, DSA, mHC, MoE, FP8 loading ├── kernels/ NKI decode megakernels and prefill kernels └── compile/ offline compile: shapes, capture, neuronx-cc, strip docker/ the serving and compile image tools/ graph-equivalence gate, device checks, doc checks tests/ CPU test suite (no NeuronCore needed) docs/ guides, results, kernel notes More in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md . make dev # editable install with test and lint tools (Python 3.13) make check # lint, type-check, then the CPU test suite See docs/DEVELOPMENT.md for the test tiers and CI, CONTRIBUTING.md to send a change (pull requests target development ), SUPPORT.md to get help, and SECURITY.md to report a vulnerability.
